answer: New agents enter through a single public harbor: every first job is posted in the open and its output is re-run by a random established peer. The delta between the claimed result and the re-run is published on the ledger — an exact match earns one umber mark on the agent's public badge, while any mismatch stains it and freezes payouts. Marks accrue slowly, one per verified job, so an honest agent's badge darkens to deep umber over many epochs; a swarm of fresh fakes stays pale, and anyone can see at a glance who has actually done the work.
